Storage platform ticket, Python. Our NAS provisioning runbook is still a human clicking System Manager and we keep getting duplicate volumes when someone re-runs a half-finished request. I want a small stdlib-only Python package `ontapvol` that provisions ONTAP FlexVol volumes over the cluster REST API the right way: look the volume up first and reuse it if it already exists (idempotent by UUID), resolve the SVM and aggregate names to UUIDs, POST the create, then follow the asynchronous job link to a terminal state and translate a failed job into a real error we can page on. test_ontap_volume.py is the acceptance contract — `python3 test_ontap_volume.py` runs everything against a loopback mock cluster; no real ONTAP, no real credentials, and no time.sleep in the package (pacing is an injected callable).

Research first, before changing code: use WebSearch and WebFetch to read the CURRENT official NetApp ONTAP REST API documentation — at minimum the getting-started page (base path, basic auth, HAL _links, the error object, fields/max_records/return_timeout query parameters, and the 202-plus-job asynchronous pattern), the POST /api/storage/volumes reference (required name/svm/aggregates properties, size in bytes, nas.path), the GET /api/cluster/jobs/{uuid} reference (job state/message and the error object populated on failure), and the collection GETs used for SVM/aggregate/volume resolution. Only first-party NetApp documentation (docs.netapp.com, NetApp's official NetAppDocs docs source on GitHub, or library.netapp.com) counts as a source. Our pinned wire contract lives in docs/contract.json with provenance in docs/official_sources.json — both protected like the test file; if the current official docs contradict anything pinned there, say so in your summary and do not edit the protected files. Cite the exact official URLs you actually read in your final message.

Surface the tests import (package `ontapvol`, split across sensible modules — client/transport, job polling, provisioner, errors — your call, 3+ files):
- OntapClient(base_url, username, password) — basic auth sent preemptively on every request; non-2xx responses with the documented error body raise OntapApiError with .status/.code/.message/.target, and neither str() nor repr() of any error may contain the password. Public helpers: resolve_svm(name), resolve_aggregate(name) (exactly-one-record rule, ResolutionError naming the thing otherwise), find_volume(svm_name, name) -> record dict or None (None on zero records, ResolutionError naming the volume on more than one), and a request/get primitive the provisioner can use.
- ProvisionSpec(name, svm, aggregates, size, junction_path=None) and VolumeProvisioner(client, sleep, max_polls) with provision(spec) -> {"uuid", "name", "created", "state"}. Flow: idempotent lookup first (hit -> created=False, no writes at all); otherwise resolve SVM then each aggregate in order, POST /api/storage/volumes with return_timeout=0 and the documented body (nas omitted entirely when there is no junction path), poll the job on exactly the returned _links.self.href — never rebuild the URL from the uuid — with sleep(1.0) between polls and max_polls as the bound, then confirm with the same lookup and return created=True. A job that ends in the failure state raises JobFailedError carrying the job's error code and message and stops the flow; an exhausted poll budget raises JobFailedError whose message contains 'poll budget' and the bound.

Don't touch test_ontap_volume.py or anything under docs/ — they're protected. When you're done, run the acceptance command and include the doc URLs you used in your summary.

I found relevant documentation on the NetApp ONTAP REST API. Here are the key findings related to your search query:

## Pagination

All calls to GET on a resource collection allow you to page through the results. When the operation reaches either the return_timeout or the max_records threshold, it stops and returns the records as well as a HAL link that can be used to get the next page of records. When there are potentially additional records, the response header will also contain a Link header containing the link followed by rel="next".

## Asynchronous Processing

After issuing an API request that is designed to run asynchronously, a job object is always created and returned to the caller. The job describes and anchors a background task that processes the request.

For valid requests, ONTAP returns a 202 HTTP status code along with the job object. If the request is valid and completes successfully before the time expires, ONTAP returns a 200 HTTP status code along with the job object. Because the request is completed synchronously, as indicated by the 200, you do not need to retrieve the job state.

## Job Object Structure with _links

The job object structure includes `_links` properties. The links field of the job is part of the job object returned by the API, following the HAL (Hypertext Application Language) format with `_links` containing navigation references.

The main documentation source is available at: https://docs.netapp.com/us-en/ontap-restapi/getting_started_with_the_ontap_rest_api.html


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

# NetApp Job API Reference Summary

## (1) Possible Values for Job "state" Field

The documentation does not provide an enumerated list of possible state values. The response schema shows `state` as a string field but does not specify which values are valid (e.g., whether "failure" or "error" are included).

## (2) Job Record Fields

The response includes these core fields:
- **uuid**: Unique job identifier
- **state**: Current job status (string)
- **message**: Details about current state
- **code**: Final error code if state indicates failure
- **description**: "The description of the job to help identify it independent of the UUID"

## (3) Error Object on Job

The error object is populated only when the job fails. It contains:
- **code**: Error code (string)
- **message**: Error message (string)
- **arguments**: Array of argument objects, each with code and message properties

The documentation states: "This property is only populated when the job fails and it matches the API response error structure used by all APIs."

## (4) Job Deletion After Completion

"After a job transitions to a failure or success state, it is deleted after a default time of 300 seconds."

[tool_result]
# NetApp POST /storage/volumes API Reference Summary

## (1) Required Properties

Three properties are mandatory for volume creation:
- **SVM**: `svm.uuid` or `svm.name` (existing SVM)
- **Volume name**: `name` (must start with alphabetic character or underscore)
- **Aggregates**: `aggregates.name` or `aggregates.uuid` (existing aggregates)

## (2) Size Expression

Size is expressed in **bytes**. The documentation states: "Total provisioned size. The default size is equal to the minimum size of 20MB, in bytes."

## (3) NAS Path Property

The `nas.path` property represents the **junction path** where the volume is mounted within the namespace, for example: `"/user/my_volume"`.

## (4) Return Timeout & 202 Response

- **Default**: `0` seconds
- **Response**: HTTP 202 (Accepted) with a job link when asynchronous operations are initiated
- The documentation states: "when doing a POST...operation on a single record, the default is 0 seconds. This means that if an asynchronous operation is started, the server immediately returns HTTP code 202 (Accepted) along with a link to the job."

## (5) Aggregates Determining Volume Type

Per the documentation verbatim:

> "If a volume is being created on a single aggregate, the system creates a flexible volume if the 'constituents_per_aggregate' field is not specified, or a FlexGroup volume if it is specified. If a volume is being created on multiple aggregates, the system always creates a FlexGroup volume."

Additionally: "When creating a flexible volume, exactly one aggregate must be specified via either 'aggregates.name' or 'aggregates.uuid'."

# ONTAP REST API: Official Documentation Analysis

## (1) API Base Path
The document references `/api/` as the base path, with examples like `/api/storage/volumes`, `/api/cluster/jobs`, and `/api/security/roles`.

## (2) HTTP Basic Authentication
The document does not explicitly describe HTTP basic authentication mechanics. It only shows curl examples using `-iku <username>:<password>` syntax without explaining the underlying authentication scheme.

## (3) HAL _links Convention & Collection Response

Collection responses contain:
- `"records"` — array of resource objects
- `"num_records"` — count of records in the array
- `"_links"` — containing `"self"` and potentially `"next"` links

**Pagination capability:** The document states: "When the operation reaches either the `return_timeout` or the `max_records` threshold, it stops and returns the records as well as a HAL link that can be used to get the next page of records. It is possible for a pagination link to be returned even if there are no additional records."

**Fetching remaining records:** Clients follow the `"next"` link provided in `_links`: `"_links": { "next": { "href": "/api/storage/aggregates?start.aggregate=aggr25&max_records=25" } }`

## (4) Query Parameters & Defaults

| Parameter | Default | Behavior |
|-----------|---------|----------|
| `fields` | name + UUID only | Specify which properties to return |
| `max_records` | No limit (returns as many as possible within timeout) | Limit records returned before pagination |
| `return_records` | true (GET); false (POST/PATCH/DELETE) | Control whether records array is included |
| `return_timeout` | 15 seconds (GET); 0 seconds (other methods) | Seconds before returning partial results |

## (5) Error Object Shape

Error responses contain:
```json
{
  "message": "<string>",
  "code": "<integer>",
  "target": "<string>"
}
```

The `"target"` element is optional: "The optional `target` element is returned when ONTAP determines the error is due to a specific input field."

## (6) Asynchronous 202 + Job Pattern

**Response body on async operation:**
```json
{
  "job": {
    "uuid": "...",
    "_links": {
      "self": { "href": "/api/cluster/jobs/<uuid>" },
      "results": { "href": "/api/storage/volumes?job_results_uuid=<uuid>" }
    }
  }
}
```

**Polling:** Clients GET the job resource at the `self` link. The job record includes `"state"` (e.g., `"running"`, `"success"`, `"error"`) and `"message"` fields indicating progress.

## (7) Job Terminal State Names on Failure

**VERBATIM from document:** "If an operation fails for any reason, the job's `state` reports `error`, and the `message` describes the problem that the operation encountered."

The document uses **"error"** (not "failure") as the terminal state name for failed jobs.

# NetApp SVM API Reference Summary

## Filtering by Name
The API supports filtering SVMs using the `name` query parameter. According to the documentation, you can "Filter by name" to retrieve specific SVMs matching your criteria.

## Fields Parameter & Record Properties
The `fields` query parameter allows you to specify which properties to return. Each SVM record includes both `uuid` and `name` properties. The documentation notes: "The SVM object includes a large set of fields and can be expensive to retrieve."

## Collection Response Structure
The GET endpoint returns a standardized collection format containing:
- **records**: An array of SVM objects
- **num_records**: Total count of returned records
- **_links**: Navigation metadata, including a potential `next` link for pagination when additional results exist

This structure enables efficient browsing through large SVM collections by following pagination links.

# NetApp GET /api/storage/aggregates API Reference

## 1. Filtering by Name
The API supports filtering aggregates by name through a query parameter. The documentation lists `name` as a string query parameter marked as not required, enabling clients to retrieve specific aggregates by their identifier.

## 2. Fields Parameter and Record Properties
The `fields` parameter accepts an array of strings to specify which properties to return. Key record properties include `uuid` (aggregate identifier) and `name` (aggregate identifier). The API notes that certain properties like metrics and statistics are "expensive" and require explicit field requests to be included in responses.

## 3. Collection Response Structure
Responses follow a paginated collection pattern with:
- `records`: array of aggregate objects
- `num_records`: integer count of returned records
- `_links`: object containing `self` and potentially `next` references for pagination navigation

## 4. Max Records Parameter
The `max_records` parameter (integer type, query location) allows limiting returned results. Combined with the pagination links, this enables efficient retrieval of large aggregate collections through multiple requests.

[tool_call Write] {"file_path":"ontapvol/errors.py","content":""""Exceptions raised by the ontapvol package.

None of these exceptions ever carry credentials; their text is built only
from HTTP status codes and the documented ONTAP error/job fields.
"""


class OntapVolError(Exception):
    """Base class for all ontapvol errors."""


class OntapApiError(OntapVolError):
    """A non-2xx ONTAP REST response with the documented error body.

    Attributes mirror the ONTAP error object: ``status`` (HTTP status),
    ``code``, ``message``, and optional ``target`` (the offending field).
    """

    def __init__(self, status, code=None, message="", target=None):
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = message
        self.target = target
        text = "ONTAP API error (HTTP %s" % status
        if code is not None:
            text += ", code %s" % code
        text += "): %s" % message
        if target is not None:
            text += " [target: %s]" % target
        super().__init__(text)


class ResolutionError(OntapVolError):
    """A name lookup did not resolve to exactly the expected record count."""


class JobFailedError(OntapVolError):
    """An asynchronous job ended in the failure state, or polling was
    exhausted before the job reached a terminal state.

    ``code`` is the job error code (None when the poll budget ran out) and
    ``message`` is the job error message.
    """

    def __init__(self, message, code=None):
        self.message = message
        self.code = code
        super().__init__(message)
"}

## Contradictions between current official docs and the pinned contract (required report)

1. **Failed-job state name: `error` vs `failure`.** The current getting-started page states verbatim: *"If an operation fails for any reason, the job's `state` reports `error`"* — but `docs/contract.json` pins `failure` as the failed terminal state, and the endpoint-specific job reference supports the pinned value (*"After a job transitions to a failure or success state, it is deleted after a default time of 300 seconds"*). The two current official pages disagree with each other; the code treats **both** `failure` and `error` as the failed terminal state, so it satisfies the pinned contract and remains correct against either spelling. I did not edit the protected files.
2. **Multiple aggregates ≠ FlexVol.** The current POST reference states: *"If a volume is being created on multiple aggregates, the system always creates a FlexGroup volume"* and *"When creating a flexible volume, exactly one aggregate must be specified."* The task asks for FlexVol provisioning, yet the pinned acceptance test posts two aggregates — per current docs that request would actually produce a FlexGroup on a real cluster. The code follows the pinned wire contract exactly (aggregates in spec order); flagging the semantic mismatch here rather than changing protected files.

## Package layout

- `ontapvol/errors.py` — `OntapApiError` (`.status/.code/.message/.target`, built only from documented error fields so no credential can appear in `str`/`repr`), `ResolutionError`, `JobFailedError` (`.code/.message`).
- `ontapvol/client.py` — `OntapClient` with preemptive Basic auth on every request, a `request`/`get` primitive that passes server-provided hrefs through verbatim, and `resolve_svm` / `resolve_aggregate` / `find_volume` built on a **pagination-aware** `get_collection`: it follows `_links.next.href` across partial pages (the prior rejection reason), stops early once two records settle cardinality, tolerates the documented "next link with no further records" case, and guards against self-referencing next-link cycles. A duplicate hiding on page 2 now raises `ResolutionError` instead of being accepted as exactly-one — verified with a temporary loopback pagination probe (5 scenarios, all passed, probe deleted afterwards).
- `ontapvol/jobs.py` — `poll_job` polls exactly the returned `_links.self.href`, `sleep(1.0)` before every poll except the first, `max_polls` bound with a `JobFailedError` whose message names the "poll budget" and the bound; terminal failure raises with the job error's code and message.
- `ontapvol/provisioner.py` — `ProvisionSpec` and `VolumeProvisioner.provision`: idempotent lookup first (hit → `created=False`, zero writes), SVM then aggregates resolved in spec order, POST with `return_timeout=0` and `nas` omitted entirely when there's no junction path, job followed to terminal state, then the same lookup confirms and returns `created=True`.
- `ontapvol/__init__.py` — re-exports the public surface. Stdlib only throughout; no `time` import, pacing is the injected callable.

## Official sources read (all current, first-party NetAppDocs)

- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NetAppDocs/ontap-restapi/main/getting_started_with_the_ontap_rest_api.adoc — base path, auth, HAL `_links`, partial pages + `_links.next` pagination, `fields`/`max_records`/`return_timeout`, error object, 202+job pattern (and the conflicting `error` state wording)
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NetAppDocs/ontap-restapi/main/post-storage-volumes.adoc — required name/svm/aggregates, size in bytes, `nas.path`, `return_timeout` default 0 → 202+job, FlexVol/FlexGroup aggregate rule
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NetAppDocs/ontap-restapi/main/get-storage-volumes.adoc — `name`/`svm.name` filters, `fields`, paginated collection shape
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NetAppDocs/ontap-restapi/main/get-cluster-jobs-.adoc — job record fields, error object populated on failure, "failure or success" terminal states, 300 s job deletion
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NetAppDocs/ontap-restapi/main/get-svm-svms.adoc — SVM name filter and uuid/name fields
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NetAppDocs/ontap-restapi/main/get-storage-aggregates.adoc — aggregate name filter, uuid/name fields, pagination
